title: YouTube Music launches new labels as AI-generated music floods streaming platforms
slides: Can YouTube Music’s new labels stop AI music?
Labels will flag AI-generated tracks on the platform.
But the system relies on artists to self-disclose.
You’ll see badges—but hidden AI still thrives.
Check for labels, but don’t trust them blindly.
thread_text:
1. AI Music Gets Labels

YouTube Music now flags AI-generated tracks, but artists must self-disclose. That leaves a loophole wide open.

2. Self-Reporting Problem

The system depends on creators admitting their songs are AI-made. No disclosure, no label.

3. Badges But No Barrier

Viewers see badges on disclosed tracks. Hidden AI tracks still slip through without any warning.

4. False Security Risk

Seeing a badge might make you trust the platform. But absence of a badge doesn't mean human-made.

5. Check, Then Question

Next time you stream, look for the label. Then ask yourself: can you really trust it? Test one track today.

script: YouTube Music now labels AI-generated tracks.

Check for labels, but don't trust blindly.

instagram.caption:
Artists have to volunteer that their music was made by AI — nobody checks for them.

YouTube Music just added labels for AI-generated tracks. The system only works if the artist admits it. No confession, no label.

So a track can be fully AI-made and show zero badges, while you assume it's human.

If you publish music, your AI track stays unlabeled unless you flag it yourself. If you're a listener, that badge means less than it looks.

Open a song you trust right now. Is the label there — or just your assumption?
